mentl/e6c4192:
Found by walking the felt path with the CLI. No .mn changed — the tree is
green; this banks the design and its RED-first gate.

THE PARSER DOES NOT KNOW WHICH MODULE IT IS IN. The driver concatenates the
dep DAG into one text and parses it whole, so every node is born in the
weave's coordinate space unattributed, and five machines exist to put back
what that throws away: the out-of-band range map; NModule nodes minted after
the parse from that map; rehome_seam_comments, whose own comment says "the
parser cannot see seams"; module_path_of_span's O(next) containment scan,
whose comment names its "O(1) destiny"; and the seam-render family
(module_seams walking every node per call, seam_of_line, span_render_local).

The symptom that surfaced it: on a SEVEN-LINE file `mentl why addr.mn double`
answers `at 2726:1-2726:21`, while the refs facet three lines away answers
`addr:7`. show_reason feeds every felt surface — LSP hover, the cursor view's
Why line, the type facet — so intent-is-walkable walks to a line nobody can
open. A translation layer every reader must remember to call is one some
reader will not call.

TWO NON-ULTIMATE FORMS BUILT AND REJECTED, both recorded. Threading seams
into show_reason fixes the symptom and entrenches the compensation — a bolt,
named in the same session that named the family. Span carrying its module
(96 sites, whole-wheel census 100) is SUFFICIENT, not ultimate: a span inside
a Reason is a copied projection of where a node is — a Frozen scheme one
layer over — and copied coordinates rot under editing, which the resident
session depends on them not doing.

THE ULTIMATE: parse per module. Module-local spans from lex, the NModule node
minted before its own parse, every node attributed at birth with the module
as a spine column. One-namespace judgment never required one TEXT, only one
ENV — parse each module, concatenate the decl lists, judge as one program.
All five compensations delete. The Reason layer follows: the dominant shape
is graph

Three finds this session were one shape. BodyContext: "read by LEvPerform's
offset arithmetic", zero readers. Delta: "the Cursor handler's
CursorView.teach field reads through delta_pick", no such field. The
drifted verify_candidate copy: "mirrors the sequential arm exactly", it did
not. A declaration nothing references, carrying prose explaining how it is
used — the prose is the evidence, because someone wrote down a belief the
graph disagrees with. Each cost a hand read to notice.

`mentl query <file> "orphan-claims"` reports the structural conjunction:
zero outside references AND 240+ bytes of attached comment, read live
through graph_comment_at. A comment is graph content, so this needed no new
column.

It deliberately does not read English. Deciding that "read by LEvPerform"
is a claim would mean parsing meaning, and a checker that guesses at
meaning would be a second, worse comment-ref tier. It names the sites; a
person reads the prose. The existing comment-ref ratchet covers the other
half at the name layer — a backticked name resolving nowhere — and it
stayed at zero through all three finds, because every phantom reader was
named without backticks. That gap is why this is a separate tier.

First run: 216 declarations. Not 216 bugs, and the residue entry says so —
type names dominate because an annotation makes no reference edge, and a
library's public vocabulary is unreferenced by the wheel by design, with
lib/threading alone contributing 25 rows.

The standout, found in one read: cursor -> ic_fixpoint_handler at 3,245
bytes of prose and zero references, the largest claim in the wheel and a
handler nothing installs anywhere. One step past Delta, which at least sat
in three chains. Banked as Hβ.cursor.ic-fixpoint-handler-is-never-installed
rather than deleted: Delta was decidable because the T_OverDeclared
diagnostic was demonstrably better, and here nothing else memoizes cursor

mentl/e6e133f:
The Snoc-tree second-truth landmine (list_pop returns last, requires
Recurse-First Topological Traversal) was costing more in subtle bugs
than the original O(N²) was costing in time. New primitive list_to_flat
materializes any list-tree to a contiguous tag=0 flat array in O(N).
Threaded into the hot-path entrances of lex, parse-prep, check, and
closure-lowering. After this, list[i] is honest in WASM — single
i32.load — and forward-index loops stay written as forward-index loops.

  std/runtime/memory.lux  list_to_flat + fill_flat + fallback
  src/vm/vm.rs            identity registration (Vec is already flat)
  std/compiler/ty.lux     builtin type signature
  std/compiler/lexer.lux  flatten chars(source) at lex entry
  std/compiler/check.lux  flatten stmts at check_program_with entry
  std/compiler/pipeline.lux  flatten between lex and parse_program
  std/compiler/lower_closure.lux  flatten at 5 hot-path entries
  std/compiler/lower.lux  list_head/list_tail → list_first/list_rest
                          (naming honesty: head/tail confuse on Snoc)
  std/backend/wasm_collect.lux  prepend → append (consistent with
                                 flatten-once direction)

mentl/e675201:
The lowerer now defaults to print_string for unknown types (instead of
print_int). In WASM, all values are heap pointers — print_string reads
bytes from the pointer, print_int formats the integer. print_string is
always correct for heap pointers.

Also removed the s ++ "" allocation in the WasmOut handler. The concat
was forcing string type coercion but allocated on every out() call,
exhausting the WASM bump heap. With the lowerer fix, print(s) directly
dispatches to print_string without the allocation.

Bootstrap output on wasmtime is 1.4MB — the compilation pipeline runs
end-to-end. String garbling after line 16 remains (WASM runtime string
representation issue, not a print dispatch issue).

stoop/e66b7c6:
Five more went at it cold and only one thing was actually broken, which
is the right ratio this late: a tablet reads fine, a scene of three keeps
its bylines through an export and an import, two issues reprint as
themselves, and a mess made and cleared comes back whole with undo.

Printing had two holes. Ctrl-P from anywhere but the press handed the
browser a blank page: the print stylesheet hides main, and nothing
populated the print zone unless you happened to be standing on the
press. Printing is about paper and paper is the imposed sheet, wherever
somebody was when the thought struck them, so the sheet is now put there
whatever is on screen. And the zone was only ever emptied by afterprint,
which not every browser fires and a cancelled dialog may not either; a
zone left populated keeps body.reprinting set, and every later print
would have reused that stale sheet for ever. It clears on a timer as
well as on the event.

Keyboard focus was invisible on the one control that is edited in place,
the zine's name in the bar, because it traded its outline for a colour
that only reads if you already knew where you were. Focus is visible
everywhere now, in the spot colour, and in red on the page itself where
a ring around a word would be noise.

On a phone the bar wrapped to two rows because the nav was told to take
a whole one. A phone knows which app it is in; the wordmark goes and the
zine's own name carries the identity, which puts the nav back on the
first row: the bar is 45px rather than 79, and the page starts 100px down
rather than 134.
